findings.evidence: dbff837f digest cut list: removed units (485, showing 40). The 40 shown paragraphs are explained by section rows in docs/audit/recovery/design-system-starter/sections.json plus record.md; the other 445 are not listed, so they cannot be ruled explained.
findings.fix: Emit the remaining 445 para ids (or confirm they are only sub-units of the recorded sections) and add a record row for any substantive unit not already covered, restoring domain templates into references/.

findings.evidence: description names DTCG .tokens.json and semantic tokens, but not the file shapes the workflow actually writes: design-tokens.json, $schema, CSS custom properties, or data-theme.
findings.fix: Set up or evolve a shared design system: semantic design tokens in a DTCG 2025.10 .tokens.json or design-tokens.json ($type, $value, $schema), CSS custom properties switched by data-theme for light and dark, reusable component APIs (atoms, molecules, organisms), contrast-checked token pairs, and versioned migration off scattered styles. Use when asked to create a design system or token file, convert raw hex, px or palette names into semantic tokens, standardize UI across apps or teams, define component library conventions, or version and deprecate shared tokens and components, even when the user only says the screens look inconsistent or all over the place. Not for reviewing or fixing one screen or component against UI rules (ui-ux-principles), one-off pages, ARIA how-to questions in an existing form, Storybook stories for existing components, SVG icon optimization, logos, or marketing copy.

findings.evidence: Step 7 says to run the theme-state check in references/component-examples.md, but does not say to load only the Theme-state validation section, and the file also holds Card, Modal, navigation and theme-toggle examples that step does not need.
findings.fix: In step 7, say to load only the Theme-state validation section of references/component-examples.md, and not the Card, Modal, navigation or theme-toggle sections, unless step 5 is also in scope.

findings.evidence: Step 6's default is data-theme CSS custom properties, but the escape hatch (Tailwind variants or a ThemeProvider) is chosen by whether the project already depends on it or needs runtime theme objects, with no tie-break when both are true.
findings.fix: Keep data-theme as the default; if both Tailwind and a ThemeProvider already exist, keep the one the consuming screens already use and record the choice in the checklist scope line.

findings.evidence: 19 trigger queries (10 should-trigger, 9 should-not), short of about 20 with 8-10 on each side, and no train/validation split.
findings.fix: Add one realistic should-not-trigger near-miss (for example a finished-token export or a one-file CSS rename) and mark a fixed 60/40 train/validation split in the query file.

findings.evidence: The contrast script's worked example says #9ca3af on #fff prints ratio 2.5388 and pass false. The same relative-luminance formula yields about 2.54 only for the darker gray #9ca3af; #9ca3af on white is about 2.74, so the printed example is not what the script prints.
findings.fix: Re-run the script on #9ca3af and #fff and replace 2.5388 and 2.54 with the printed ratio and display values, keeping pass false.

findings.evidence: The naming rule says color.semantic.border.default becomes --color-border by dropping trailing default, but the deprecation example is rooted at color.action.default with no semantic segment, which the same rule would emit as --color-action-default, not --color-action.
findings.fix: State the rule for both shapes: a token under color.semantic drops semantic and a trailing default or ring, while a theme file rooted at color.action.default maps to --color-action.
